title.en: 'My only son was shot standing up for justice' - inside city gripped by deadly protests in Pakistan-administered Kashmir
title.zh: “我唯一的儿子为了正义而被枪杀”——在巴控克什米尔发生致命抗议的城市内

summary.en: The BBC gains unique access to Rawalakot, scene of violent clashes between security forces and protesters in Pakistan-administered Kashmir.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及公义、尊严与问责。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Dr Anwar's makeshift clinic is not far from the main protest site in the city of Rawalakot in Pakistan-administered Kashmir (PAK). A spare bedroom acts as a medical supply cupboard, outside is a bed under a red stretched tarpaulin.

Lying across the bed is Shafqat Hussain, shot in the chest. The sheet he lies on is already stained with the blood of previously injured. He is dying.

In the last two months, dozens of people have been killed across the region in clashes between security officials and protesters from the group Joint Awami Action Committee (JAAC).

This region - home to about 4.5 million people - currently has elections taking place .

The BBC is the first media organisation to gain access to Rawalakot and speak to those at the heart of the protests.

Dr Anwar – whose name, like most of those in this report, has been changed to protect contributors – tells our team: "We have enough supplies to provide first aid. We can stop bleeding, clean and dress wounds, and remove superficial bullets. But patients with serious injuries to the chest, abdomen, head, or other vital organs need advanced hospitals."

Anwar adds: "Even major hospitals would struggle if many such patients arrived at the same time."

Since 27 July, the clinic has treated around 50 to 60 critically injured patients, the doctor says, adding that he personally treated 15 to 20 with gunshot wounds.

Protesters are scared to go to the main hospital because they fear they will be arrested or shot. The authorities have said that claim is inaccurate.

"Most of those who have been killed or seriously injured are young people between about 15-16 years old and 32-35 years old. I have seen very few patients over the age of 40."

"We only asked for affordable flour, electricity and our basic rights," he says, trying to steady his breath through his sobs. "Instead, our brothers are being killed. What was our crime? Why are live bullets being fired at us?"

Protesters from the JAAC say the demonstrations are about their rights, with concerns including electricity prices, education and health care. An agreement signed with the Pakistan and PAK governments back in October was meant to help. The JAAC says it's not been implemented.

The local government disagrees. They say the group is armed and that this is about disrupting the ongoing polls. And they are not willing to let the protesters march to the regional capital, Muzaffarabad.

The JAAC was banned in June; they have been labelled foreign-funded terrorists. They reject this characterisation, saying they are peaceful and - though funded from the PAK community abroad - not sponsored by India.

Rather than initiating violence, they say they are the victims and that Pakistan's security forces have been firing on them.

title.en: US and Japan take action to prop up yen in rare joint move
title.zh: 美日罕见联合行动以支撑日元

summary.en: The United States and Japan have announced a rare joint intervention to stabilize the yen, indicating their readiness to take further coordinated action if needed.
summary.zh: 美国和日本宣布采取罕见的联合行动以稳定日元汇率，并表示未来将毫不犹豫地进行联合干预。

body.en:
Japan and the US have confirmed that they jointly intervened last week to halt a slide in the yen after it weakened to a fresh 40-year low.

The joint intervention is the first since 2011, when both countries took coordinated action to weaken the yen after the devastating earthquake and tsunami that hit eastern Japan.

Both Japan's Ministry of Finance and US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent have said that they will not hesitate to conduct more joint interventions in the future.

It highlights both countries' efforts to prevent a sell-off in the yen and Japanese government bonds from having an impact on the global economy, including potentially helping to push up borrowing costs for Washington.

"The United States agreed to participate in the coordinated intervention because it serves its national interests by offering the prospect of significant benefits at a low cost," Shigeto Nagai, head of Japan economics at Oxford Economics told the BBC.

The two countries are expected to continue to intervene "intermittently in a coordinated manner for some time", he added.

"Even if the actual amount of intervention is not particularly large, the prolonged sense of vigilance regarding intervention will be effective in deterring speculators."

The yen is historically weak mainly due to Japan having much lower central bank interest rates than other major economies like the US. That makes the Japanese currency less attractive to international investors.

The Bank of Japan last raised interest rates in June, as it increased its main rate to 1% - the highest level since September 1995. In comparison, the US Federal Reserve's benchmark rate is in a range of 3.50% to 3.75%.

Japan also faces other issues including a decades-long slide in its working-age population, low productivity and a heavy reliance on energy imports that are priced in US dollars.

On Monday, Japan's finance ministry said Friday's intervention with the US Treasury Department "countered excessive volatility and disorderly movements in the Japanese yen in recent months".

The "coordinated foreign exchange actions countered disorderly yen movements," Bessent said in a social media post.

"We strongly support Japan's decisive market and monetary steps to correct the substantial undervaluation of the yen," he added.

"They have a weakening yen, and they wanted a little bit of help. And we're always there for Japan," US President Donald Trump told reporters on Sunday.

The dollar fell by 0.2% to 157.07 yen after Trump's comments, well off the 40-year high of 164 last month, but rose back to 157.70 yen after the Japanese finance ministry's statement.

body.zh: 日本和美国已确认上周联合干预，以阻止日元跌至 40 年来的新低后的下滑。 此次联合干预是自2011年以来的首次，当时两国在日本东部发生毁灭性地震和海啸后采取协调行动压低日元汇率。 日本财务省和美国财长斯科特·贝森特均表示，未来将毫不犹豫地进行更多联合干预。 它凸显了两国为防止日元和日本政府债券抛售对全球经济产生影响而做出的努力，包括可能有助于推高华盛顿的借贷成本。 牛津经济研究院日本经济学负责人永井茂人告诉英国广播公司：“美国同意参与协调干预，因为它可以以低成本提供显着利益的前景，从而符合其国家利益。” 他补充说，预计两国将继续“在一段时间内以协调的方式间歇性地进行干预”。 “即使实际的干预量不是特别大，但对干预的长期警惕感也会有效震慑投机者。” 日元历史上疲软的主要原因是日本央行利率远低于美国等其他主要经济体。这使得日元对国际投资者的吸引力下降。 日本央行上次加息是在6月，将主要利率提高至1%，为1995年9月以来的最高水平。相比之下，美联储的基准利率在3.50%至3.75%之间。 日本还面临其他问题，包括劳动年龄人口长达数十年的下滑、生产率低下以及严重依赖以美元计价的能源进口。 日本财务省周一表示，周五对美国财政部的干预“遏制了日元近几个月来的过度波动和无序波动”。 贝森特在社交媒体上发帖称，“协调一致的外汇行动对抗了日元的无序波动”。 他补充说：“我们强烈支持日本采取果断的市场和货币措施，以纠正日元大幅低估的情况。” “他们的日元走弱，他们需要一点帮助。我们始终支持日本，”美国总统唐纳德·特朗普周日告诉记者。 特朗普发表言论后，美元兑日元下跌0.2%，至157.07日元，远低于上个月164的40年高点，但在日本财务省发表声明后，美元兑日元回升至157.70日元。 日本央行数据显示，东京周四干预纽约市场时，可能已抛售近 590 亿美元购买日元。

reflection.en: In complex global economics, the decision by the US and Japan to act together highlights the importance of seeking broad counsel. When nations collaborate on major policy decisions, it underscores the wisdom found in collective guidance for the well-being of their people and the global economy.
reflection.zh: 在复杂的全球经济中，美国和日本决定共同行动，凸显了寻求广泛建议的重要性。当国家就重大政策决策进行合作时，这强调了为两国人民和全球经济福祉而寻求集体指导的智慧。

verse.textEn: For lack of guidance a nation falls, but victory is won through many advisers.
verse.textZh: 无智谋，民就败落；谋士多，人便安居。

title.en: 'Deeply saddened': Australian helicopter provider speaks after Greece firefighting tragedy
title.zh: “深感悲痛”：澳大利亚直升机供应商就希腊消防悲剧发表声明

summary.en: McDermott Aviation, an Australian helicopter provider, expressed profound sadness following a tragedy involving one of its leased helicopters in Greece, where wildfires continue to spread across southern Europe.
summary.zh: 澳大利亚直升机供应商麦克德莫特航空对在希腊发生的一起悲剧深表悲痛，该公司曾向希腊租赁直升机，以应对持续蔓延的南欧野火。

body.en:
Two crew members have died after two helicopters — leased by Australian company McDermott Aviation — collided midair while battling wildfires in Greece on Sunday.

A Greek and a Danish national were killed in the crash over Psatha, an area west of Athens, according to Greece's fire service. Two crew members from Greece and Britain who were operating a separate helicopter were found alive.

Founder and president of McDermott Aviation, John McDermott said he was "deeply saddened" by news of the fatal collision.

"We are deeply saddened to confirm that the two crew members aboard one of the helicopters have lost their lives. The two crew members from the second helicopter are in the care of medical professionals.

"Our thoughts and deepest condolences are with the families, friends and colleagues of those affected by this tragic incident. Both crews were undertaking the critical work of supporting firefighting operations to help protect communities."

McDermott Aviation has reportedly operated in Greece for several years. The company said it is working closely with relevant authorities as they undertake an investigation into the cause of the incident.

Over the past decade, McDermott Aviation said it has engaged in around 10 to 12 international movements a year via sea and air freight. It also operates in New Caledonia, Papua New Guinea, Indonesia and the United States, which is currently experiencing wildfires in several western states.

Nikos Pagiotelis has been a volunteer firefighter in Greece for more than 20 years. He told SBS Greek about the moment he heard news of the crash over local radio.

"When you are inside the fire, and you are trying to help the people, you're trying to save the animals, save the forest. Then suddenly [you] hear that two helicopters have crashed a couple of miles near you — you can understand that something really hurts inside," Pagiotelis said.

"You can do nothing, you freeze for a little bit, and then you just continue your work. You continue to help people to honour the lives of the loss of two comrades."

In a statement on social media, Greek prime minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis also expressed his "sorrow for the tragic accident" and extended condolences to the families of the deceased firefighters.

"The loss of the Greek coordinator and the Danish pilot at the time they were attempting the major fire in Porto Gremeno fills us all with grief," Mitsotakis said.

Nearly 500 firefighters and 23 aircraft have been deployed to fight fires in Greece, which have been driven by high temperatures and gale-force winds.

title.en: Malaysian boy on trial for allegedly murdering girl in school
title.zh: 马来西亚男孩因涉嫌在学校谋杀女孩而受审

summary.en: The high-profile case has shocked Malaysia and sparked debate about the effect of social media on children.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及公义、尊严与问责。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
A teenage boy in Malaysia is on trial for allegedly killing a female schoolmate, in a high-profile case that has sparked debate about the effects of social media on children.

The boy is accused of murdering 16-year-old Yap Shing Xuen last October. The girl was found fatally stabbed multiple times in a toilet at their secondary school on the outskirts of the capital Kuala Lumpur.

The boy, who was 14 at the time, has pleaded not guilty. If convicted, he could spend decades in prison.

Police previously said they suspected social media could have influenced the boy.

Police also confirmed a note was found on him at the time of his arrest. Reports about the note's alleged content have fueled the wider discussion about the role of social media.

Under Malaysian law, the boy cannot be publicly identified as he is still a minor.

His young age also means he will not face the death penalty if found guilty. However he could still face 30 to 40 years in jail, and he could also be flogged. The age of criminal responsibility in Malaysia is 10 years old.

The case has profoundly shocked the country and triggered a nationwide conversation about the negative effects of social media on children, particularly exposure to the manosphere and incel culture.

Some have compared the case to the Netflix series Adolescence, which explores similar themes involving teenage boys, online radicalisation and violence.

Last year Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim was asked about the case as well as other recent cases of violence in schools.

He was quoted by local media as saying that "almost all of these issues stem from the use of mobile phones and social media", and vowed to look into stricter measures.

Authorities have since put in place new rules which they say will protect children and reduce their exposure to harmful online content.

Since June, Malaysia has banned all children under the age of 16 from having accounts on major social media platforms.
body.zh: 马来西亚一名少年因涉嫌杀害一名女同学而受到审判，这起案件备受瞩目，引发了关于社交媒体对儿童影响的争论。 这名男孩被指控去年 10 月谋杀了 16 岁的叶成学。这名女孩被发现在首都吉隆坡郊区中学的厕所里被多刀刺死。 这名男孩当时14岁，现已不认罪。如果罪名成立，他可能会在监狱里度过几十年。 警方此前表示，他们怀疑社交媒体可能影响了这名男孩。 警方还证实，在他被捕时在他身上发现了一张纸条。有关该便条涉嫌内容的报道引发了有关社交媒体作用的更广泛讨论。 根据马来西亚法律，这名男孩还未成年，因此不能公开其身份。 他的年龄还很年轻，这也意味着如果罪名成立，他不会面临死刑。然而，他仍可能面临30至40年的监禁，并且还可能受到鞭打。马来西亚的刑事责任年龄是10岁。 此案震惊了全国，并引发了一场全国性的讨论，讨论社交媒体对儿童的负面影响，特别是接触男性圈和非独身文化。 一些人将此案与 Netflix 的剧集《青春期》进行比较，该剧探讨了类似的主题，涉及十几岁的男孩、网络激进化和暴力。 去年，安瓦尔·易卜拉欣总理被问及此案以及最近发生的其他学校暴力案件。 当地媒体援引他的话说，“几乎所有这些问题都源于手机和社交媒体的使用”，并誓言要采取更严格的措施。 当局此后制定了新规则，他们称这些规则将保护儿童并减少他们接触有害在线内容的机会。 自6月起，马来西亚禁止所有16岁以下儿童在主要社交媒体平台上拥有账户。

reflection.en: This story draws attention to justice, dignity, and accountability. Micah 6:8 reminds us to meet sharp headlines with justice tempered by mercy, asking how faithful people can respond with wisdom instead of noise.

title.en: Massive Attack respond after Singapore ban over Palestine display
title.zh: 新加坡禁止巴勒斯坦展示后大规模攻击回应

summary.en: The UK band says they are "surprised and disappointed" by their treatment over shouting "free Palestine" at a concert there.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Massive Attack have said they were "surprised and disappointed" by their treatment by Singaporean authorities after expressing pro-Palestine sentiments during a performance in the city-state.

The group wrote on Instagram on Sunday that its members were "detained by the police, isolated and separately questioned", with some subject to hotel room searches and temporary passport confiscation.

The band's two members held up a Palestinian flag during its 29 July show there and shouted "free Palestine" alongside members of the audience.

Singapore, which has stringent rules on public speech and assembly, subsequently said it had indefinitely banned Massive Attack from returning to the country.

A police spokeswoman told the BBC on Friday that the two band members would not be allowed to re-enter Singapore and were barred from performing there.

Robert Del Naja and Grant Marshall were "given stern warnings" concerning alleged offences under two laws that restrict the public display of foreign flags and regulate political expressions at public events.

Massive Attack said that before the show and again at the end "large sections of the auditorium organically led chants of 'Free Palestine', presumably aware but undeterred that this spontaneous expression alone could violate their government's censorship laws".

The band did not address the ban directly, but described the situation as a "surreal experience" and said they "did not imagine that merely holding up the flag of a sovereign state recognised by 157 countries would violate any law".

They added that they were "proud to have made the impromptu expression" with fans in Singapore, who "clearly felt a moral imperative to show solidarity with the people of Palestine".

The band's Instagram post, which has been liked by 146,000 users, was flooded with supportive messages from fans.

"Many of us in Singapore have grown up learning to be careful with what we say, how loudly we say it, and when it's safer to stay silent," wrote one Instagram user.

"Thank you for standing with Palestine... and for showing us that integrity can still take centre stage."

Crystal Lim-Lange, a content creator in Singapore who attended the concert, wrote in an Instagram post that this was a "complex issue".

She said she believed "artists should respect the laws of the countries they perform in".

"However, I also believe art has always challenged ideas, reflected society and sparked difficult conversations. Trying to separate art from politics has never been straightforward."

Massive Attack are known for openly expressing their political stance on a range of issues, including the war in Gaza.

body.zh: Massive Attack 表示，他们在新加坡的一场演出中表达了亲巴勒斯坦的情绪后，对新加坡当局的待遇感到“惊讶和失望”。 该组织周日在 Instagram 上写道，其成员“被警方拘留、隔离并单独审问”，其中一些人遭到酒店房间搜查和临时没收护照。 乐队的两名成员在 7 月 29 日的演出中举起了巴勒斯坦国旗，并与观众一起高喊“自由巴勒斯坦”。 对公共言论和集会有严格规定的新加坡随后表示，无限期禁止大规模袭击事件返回该国。 警方发言人周五告诉英国广播公司，这两名乐队成员将不被允许重新进入新加坡，并被禁止在那里表演。 罗伯特·德尔·纳贾和格兰特·马歇尔因涉嫌违反两项限制公开展示外国国旗和规范公共活动中政治表达的法律而受到“严厉警告”。 《大规模攻击》表示，演出前和演出结束时，“礼堂的大部分区域有机地高呼‘自由巴勒斯坦’，他们大概意识到但并没有被吓倒，这种自发的表达本身就可能违反政府的审查法”。 乐队没有直接提及禁令，但将这种情况描述为“超现实的体验”，并表示他们“没想到仅仅举起一个被 157 个国家承认的主权国家的旗帜就会违反任何法律”。 他们补充说，他们对新加坡的粉丝“做出即兴表达感到自豪”，他们“显然感到有必要向巴勒斯坦人民表示声援”。 该乐队的 Instagram 帖子获得了 146,000 名用户的点赞，其中充斥着来自粉丝的支持信息。 一位 Instagram 用户写道：“新加坡的许多人在成长过程中都学会了要小心自己的言论、说话的声音以及何时保持沉默更安全。” “感谢您与巴勒斯坦站在一起......并向我们展示诚信仍然可以占据中心舞台。” 参加音乐会的新加坡内容创作者 Crystal Lim-Lange 在 Instagram 上发帖称，这是一个“复杂的问题”。 她说她相信“艺术家应该尊重他们表演所在国家的法律”。 “然而，我也相信艺术总是挑战思想、反映社会并引发艰难的对话。试图将艺术与政治分开从来都不是一件容易的事。” 大规模攻击以在包括加沙战争在内的一系列问题上公开表达政治立场而闻名。 德尔纳贾今年早些时候因涉嫌在一次活动中表现出对被禁组织巴勒斯坦行动的支持而被捕。

reflection.en: This story draws attention to peace-making and restraint. Matthew 5:9 reminds us to meet sharp headlines with mercy, truth, and restraint, asking how faithful people can respond with wisdom instead of noise.

title.en: Two crew killed after firefighting helicopters collide in Greece, as British pilot survives
title.zh: 希腊消防直升机相撞，两名机组人员遇难，英国飞行员幸存

summary.en: Two crew members, one Danish and one Greek national, died when firefighting helicopters collided in Greece. A British pilot and another Greek crew member survived the incident.
summary.zh: 在希腊发生的一起消防直升机相撞事故中，两名机组人员——一名丹麦籍和一名希腊籍——不幸遇难。一名英国籍飞行员和另一名希腊籍机组人员幸存。

body.en:
Two crew members have been killed after two helicopters collided mid-air in Greece while battling wildfires.

The fatalities were a Danish pilot and a Greek fire service liaison officer. A British pilot and another Greek co-ordinator on the second helicopter survived.

Video of the incident some 65 km (42 miles) west of the capital Athens shows one of the two Bell helicopters hitting the rotors of the other, which bursts into flames and crashes in a ravine. The other aircraft made an emergency landing.

Wildfires have broken out in Greece this week, prompting mass evacuations. Other European states have also suffered devastating blazes during prolonged heatwaves.

According to the Greek Fire Service, the two Bell helicopters leased from Australian company McDermott Aviation collided on Sunday while taking part in efforts to tackle a large wildfire burning on the Attica-Boeotia border.

The crew members of one aircraft were rescued alive, while the second crew were recovered unconscious and later pronounced dead.

Greek Prime Minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis expressed his "deepest sorrow" over the accident.

In a post on X, he said the loss of the Greek coordinator and Danish pilot "fills us all with grief". He also sent condolences to their families.

According to protocol, all Bell helicopters across the country have been grounded, a source from the civil protection ministry told the BBC.

The source added that the second Bell helicopter involved in the collision made an emergency landing in an area of low vegetation.

"The two people on board, a British pilot and a Greek fire service liaison officer - escaped with minor injuries," the source said.

"Both remained conscious and have been admitted to hospital, where they will remain under observation for 24 hours as a precaution."

The source also told the BBC the British survivor was a private pilot hired for the wildfire season.

He was not part of any exchange between the UK and Greece, and there was no request for assistance from Athens.

Meanwhile, Greece's Ekathimerini news website said the two survivors immediately reported the collision, guiding rescuers to the crash site.

John McDermott, the founder and president of McDermott Aviation, said his staff's "thoughts and deepest condolences are with the families, friends and colleagues of those affected by this tragic incident."

"McDermott Aviation is working closely with the relevant authorities and will continue to assist as they undertake their investigation into the incident," he added.

body.en:
The body of Scottish national Elisabeth-Jane Ross was discovered last month in a suitcase in a derelict building in Athens.

A 26-year-old man has been arrested by Greek police in connection with the death of a British woman whose body was found in a suitcase in Athens last month.

"Officers of the Directorate for Combating Organized Crime have solved the homicide of a 38-year-old UK national, whose body was found inside a suitcase in an abandoned building in the Kypseli area on July 18," the Hellenic Police said on Sunday.

The victim, identified in British and Greek media reports as 38-year-old Elisabeth-Jane Ross from Scotland, arrived in Greece in late June and was last known to be in the Athens area on July 10. She was later reported missing.

Police said the suspect, a foreign national, confessed on Thursday and now faces charges including intentional homicide, robbery and firearms-related offenses.

"It emerged that the [suspect] placed the body in a suitcase and transported it to the abandoned premises. Furthermore, in the days that followed, the 26-year-old used the victim's bank cards to withdraw sums of money," police said.

According to reports, the suspect said the victim was already dead when he found her, although police made no mention of this in their statement.

Greek police said international cooperation, including support from Interpol authorities in the US and UK law enforcement agencies, helped identify the victim despite advanced decomposition.

Israeli airstrikes hit Gaza for a second straight day on Monday, killing at least 18 Palestinians, medics said, despite US President Donald Trump's announcement of a breakthrough in efforts to implement last year's ceasefire agreement.

From dawn, Israeli warplanes hit Gaza City in the north, the central city of Deir al-Balah and the southern area of Khan Younis, causing the biggest daily death toll in weeks, according to Palestinian health officials.

Trump's assertion on Friday that Palestinian Hamas militants and other armed groups had agreed to disarm had raised hopes of a turning point in efforts to end the conflict.

On Sunday, Israeli Energy Minister Eli Cohen — a member of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's security cabinet — said the government would give Hamas the opportunity to disarm but that he was "very sceptical" that would happen.

Cohen told Israel's Army Radio there had been no deal to halt attacks on Gaza and that he saw a need for Israel, which already controls 70% of the enclave, to take full control of it if Hamas did not disarm.

body.en:
US President Donald Trump says new negotiations with Iran will begin on Monday, after he decided to hold off on striking the Islamic republic to pursue a deal to end the war that's now entering its sixth month.

Trump told reporters on Monday that the talks would cover the Strait of Hormuz — a route for global energy supplies that has become a key sticking point in the conflict — and ultimately, the de-nuclearisation of Iran.

For its part, Iran said it was nearing a deal with Oman over a new route through the strait, where a tanker reported an explosion nearby on Monday, underscoring the continued volatility of the strategic waterway.

The US and Iran have been at war since 28 February, when the US and Israel launched surprise strikes against Iran, though months of on-off diplomacy have led to periods of relative calm.

Following a return to strikes last month, fears had mounted that the fighting could escalate once again. Trump had threatened to hit Iran "very hard" and was reportedly considering renewed attacks, including against energy infrastructure, with US embassies across the region on alert.

Trump pulled back from that threat Saturday, saying the "perimeters" of a deal were there.

"Now what we're doing is we're talking to them in the form of a negotiation. It begins tomorrow afternoon," Trump told reporters aboard Air Force One on Sunday, without providing details of the venue or participants in the talks.

The US president said he had been asked by Iran as well as US partners Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates and Qatar to hold off on the strikes, which he claimed would have been "the biggest attack since World War II".

A previous ceasefire deal that included the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz fell through, and Iran has since tightened its control over the waterway.

The US president said at the start of the conflict that the war was necessary to deal with Iran's nuclear program. Western nations accuse Iran of seeking a bomb, though Iran insists the program is entirely civilian in nature.

Iranian politician Hassan Ghashghavi, spokesman for the parliament's national security commission, said on Sunday that mediators were trying to revive the so-called Islamabad memorandum of understanding, which was agreed in June.

That memorandum was not intended as a final peace deal, but as a stepping stone to negotiations on a comprehensive agreement, though it did include provisions on Hormuz.

"They know that the main issue and, in fact, the key to the matter right now is the issue of the Strait of Hormuz, so yes, there is an exchange of views," Ghashghavi said.

title.en: Small insects, big damage: The global ant trade is booming
title.zh: 小昆虫，大危害：全球蚂蚁贸易蓬勃发展

summary.en: Legal or not, the trade in African ants bound for Europe is booming. What do hobbyists find appealing about these insects, and what risks does the trade pose to ecosystems, including power outages?
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及管家责任、供应与公共福祉。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Legal or not, the trade in African ants bound for Europe is booming. What do hobbyists find appealing about these insects, and what risks does the trade pose to ecosystems, including power outages?

They are unusual pieces of evidence that regularly appear in Kenyan  courtrooms: thousands of ants packed into tiny containers.

Since 2025, such finds have been presented in court several times. Staff from the Kenya Wildlife Service discovered them during baggage inspections. In multiple cases, they identified thousands of specimens of the sought-after Messor Cephalotes species also known as the Giant African Harvester Ant . A single queen can fetch more than €200 ($230) on the market.

The export of wild animals is generally prohibited in Kenya. Due to high levels of poaching — particularly involving elephants and rhinoceroses — many African countries have introduced tough laws against wildlife trafficking.

Kenya has also tightened its legislation. Under these rules, a Chinese  national who attempted to export ants was sentenced last April to one year in prison for biopiracy. Given the growing scale of smuggling and its ecological consequences , the judge said the sentence should serve as a deterrent.

It was already the second major ant-smuggling case in 12 months. The previous year, the wildlife service stopped four men who referred to themselves as the "Ant Gang." Among them were two 19-year-old Belgians  who were trying to smuggle 5,500 queens to Europe. They were fined around €5,000 each.

Whenever such cases arise, authorities often call entomologist Dino Martins to the airport. "I was shocked," he said. "Not only by the sheer number of ants, but also because they were queen ants."

The seized insects were young queens that had been dug up from nests in the ground, according to Martins, who has led several research institutes in Kenya and is regarded as one of Africa's leading ant experts, These queens have wings that allow them to fly away and establish new colonies.

"When you collect queens at this critical moment, you interrupt a key stage in the creation of new colonies," he said, adding that Kenya's ecosystems are also affected because ants transport grass seeds, helping to regenerate the savannah.

In Europe, keeping ants as pets has become increasingly popular, particularly among young people. Colonies are housed in glass terrariums where a queen produces offspring and establishes an entirely new population.

One person who keeps ants as a hobby is Michael Meier, who asked not to be identified by his real name. While at university, he wanted a pet that required little attention.

"With ants, it doesn't really matter whether I feed them today or tomorrow," he said.

body.zh: 无论合法与否，运往欧洲的非洲蚂蚁贸易正在蓬勃发展。爱好者们对这些昆虫有什么吸引力，这种贸易会给生态系统带来哪些风险，包括停电？ 它们是肯尼亚法庭上经常出现的不寻常证据：数千只蚂蚁被装在小容器里。 自 2025 年以来，此类调查结果已多次提交法庭。肯尼亚野生动物管理局的工作人员在行李检查时发现了它们。在多个案例中，他们鉴定了数千个备受追捧的 Messor Cephalotes 物种（也称为巨型非洲收割蚁）的标本。单个蜂王在市场上的售价可以超过 200 欧元（230 美元）。 肯尼亚普遍禁止出口野生动物。由于偷猎现象严重（特别是涉及大象和犀牛），许多非洲国家都出台了严厉的法律来打击野生动物贩运。 肯尼亚还加强了立法。根据这些规定，去年四月，一名试图出口蚂蚁的中国公民因生物剽窃被判处一年监禁。鉴于走私规模不断扩大及其对生态造成的影响，法官表示，该判决应起到威慑作用。 这已是12个月内第二起重大蚂蚁走私案。去年，野生动物服务部门拦住了四名自称“蚂蚁帮”的男子。其中有两名 19 岁的比利时人，他们试图将 5,500 名王后走私到欧洲。他们每人被罚款约 5,000 欧元。 每当出现此类情况时，当局通常会叫昆虫学家迪诺·马丁斯到机场。 “我很震惊，”他说。 “不仅因为蚂蚁的数量庞大，还因为它们是蚁后。” 马丁斯表示，被查获的昆虫是从地下巢穴中挖出来的年轻蚁后。马丁斯曾领导过肯尼亚多家研究机构，被认为是非洲领先的蚂蚁专家之一。这些蚁后拥有翅膀，可以让它们飞走并建立新的蚁群。 他说：“当你在这个关键时刻收集蚁后时，你就中断了新蚁群创建的关键阶段。”他补充说，肯尼亚的生态系统也会受到影响，因为蚂蚁会运输草籽，帮助大草原的再生。 在欧洲，饲养蚂蚁作为宠物越来越受欢迎，尤其是在年轻人中。蜂群被安置在玻璃容器中，蜂王在那里产下后代并建立一个全新的种群。 迈克尔·梅尔 (Michael Meier) 是一位以饲养蚂蚁为爱好的人，他要求不透露自己的真实姓名。在大学期间，他想要一只不需要太多照顾的宠物。 “对于蚂蚁来说，我今天或明天喂它们并不重要，”他说。 迈尔曾一度在一个……中饲养了近 30 个菌落。

title.en: Moscow restaurant blast a 'brutal terror attack,' mayor says
title.zh: 莫斯科市长称餐厅爆炸为“残酷恐怖袭击”

summary.en: An explosion outside an upscale Moscow restaurant at Kudrinskaya Square, described by Mayor Sergei Sobyanin as a "brutal terror attack," resulted in fatalities. The mayor vowed that those responsible would be punished, though many questions about the incident remain unanswered.
summary.zh: 莫斯科市长谢尔盖·索比亚宁称，库德林斯卡亚广场一家高档餐厅外发生的致命爆炸是“残酷的恐怖袭击”，并承诺将惩罚肇事者。然而，关于此事件的许多问题仍未解决。

body.en:
The deadly explosion outside an upscale Moscow restaurant at Kudrinskaya Square was a "brutal terror attack," Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin said, promising the perpetrators would be punished. But many questions remain.

An explosion at a restaurant in central Moscow killed at least three people, including the suspected bomber on Saturday night, authorities said.

"Law enforcement agencies are investigating the circumstances of the incident. Those responsible for this crime will certainly be found and face the punishment they deserve," he said in an online post on Sunday.

Russia's Anti-Terrorism Committee said a woman carrying  "a homemade explosive device" tried to enter the restaurant on Kudrinskaya Square but was stopped by a security guard.

The device exploded at the entrance, killing the woman, the guard and a restaurant patron.

State news agency RIA Novosti reported that at least 21 other people were injured in the blast, which occurred shortly before 8 p.m. local time (5 p.m. UTC).

The restaurant's website said the venue had been closed on Saturday for a private event.

Heavily armed law enforcement officers sealed off the area and launched an investigation.

Authorities did not immediately identify those they believed to be behind the attack.

Russia has faced several attacks since the start of the war in Ukraine in 2022. They blamed a ‌series of assassinations and attempted killings on Kyiv. Russian officials have yet to comment on any possible Ukrainian involvement into the Kudrinskaya Square blast.

However, Ukraine used drones to attack other parts of Russia on Saturday evening and early on Sunday, including a bombing which targeted an apartment block and killed two in the city Engels, some 900 kilometers (560 miles) southeast of Moscow.

Russia's Defense Ministry also said Kyiv struck a warehouse belonging to Wildberries, a major online retailer in Russia, with the Ukrainian drones hitting a site in the Samara Oblast, deep inside Russian territory. Regional Governor Vyacheslav Fedorishchev said it was not immediately clear if there were any casualties.

Russian officials also reported over a 100 Ukrainian strikes in the Belgorod Oblast, which borders Ukraine. They said Kyiv forces used artillery, rocket launchers, and drones, leaving 14 people injured.

Over 200 Ukrainian drones have allegedly been shot down during the wave of attacks.

Meanwhile, at least one person was killed and seven wounded in the Russian attack on Ukraine's Kherson, with the attack involving artillery fire.

In Dnipro, seven passengers were wounded in a drone strike on a minibus, with the regional military administrator Oleksandr Hanzha describing it as a "deliberate and cynical attack on civilians."

reflection.en: In the wake of such a brutal act, the natural human response can be to seek retribution in kind. Yet, Yahweh's word calls us to a different path, reminding us not to be overcome by evil, but to actively overcome evil with good. This challenges us to seek justice and peace in ways that break cycles of violence rather than perpetuate them.
reflection.zh: 在如此残酷的行径之后，人类自然的反应可能是以牙还牙。然而，雅伟的话语呼召我们走一条不同的道路，提醒我们不要被恶所胜，反要以善胜恶。这挑战我们以打破而非延续暴力循环的方式寻求公义与和平。

verse.textEn: Do not be overcome by evil, but overcome evil with good.

title.en: Five dead, 41 missing in Indonesia ferry fire
title.zh: 印度尼西亚渡轮火灾致五人死亡，41人失踪

summary.en: Five people have died and 41 are missing after a passenger ferry caught fire off the coast of South Sulawesi, Indonesia, marking the country's second ferry accident in two months.
summary.zh: 印度尼西亚南苏拉威西省望加锡市附近发生一起客运渡轮火灾，造成五人死亡，41人失踪，这是该国两个月内发生的第二起渡轮事故。

body.en:
Five people have been killed and 41 are ‌still missing after a ‌ferry caught fire off Indonesia's Madura island, the country's search and rescue agency says .

⁠The Mutiara Santos 2 was carrying 271 passengers and crew members, with 225 people rescued, said the regional Surabaya Search and Rescue Agency on Sunday evening. A search ⁠and ‌rescue operation is ongoing.

The ferry ‌was heading from Surabaya in East Java province to Makassar city in South Sulawesi.

It was unclear how it caught ‌fire. Madura island is located off the northeastern coast of Java. Java and Madura are next to Bali.

Basarnas, Indonesia's National Search and Rescue Agency also said some passengers jumped into the sea and were picked up by a nearby ship. Four other vessels were on standby near the ferry but could not approach because of the risk posed by flammable material on the ferry.

The captain had called the ferry company to report the fire but had not been in contact since, Basarnas added.

A larger rescue operation was heading to the site from Surabaya, a six-hour journey from the site of the disaster, Basarnas said.

"Based on preliminary reports from the field, passengers are waiting to be evacuated by the vessels in the vicinity of the incident site," Muhammad Masyhud, a senior official at the Ministry of Transportation, said in a statement.

"The safety of passengers and crew is our top priority. We are continuously coordinating with all relevant parties to ensure that the evacuation process can proceed quickly, safely, and effectively."

Marine accidents are a regular occurrence in Indonesia , an archipelago of more than 17,000 islands, partly due to lax safety standards and unpredictable weather.

A ferry transporting more than 70 people sank last month while sailing near Selayar, a small tropical island south of the much larger Sulawesi. At least four people were found dead, and 14 others remained missing until the end of the search operation.

Yet, the Scriptures offer a future hope where Yahweh himself will wipe away every tear, and death, sorrow, crying, and pain will be no more. This promise anchors our hearts even amidst present grief.
reflection.zh: 这起海上渡轮火灾造成人员伤亡和失踪的悲剧性新闻，提醒我们此类事件所带来的深切悲痛。然而，圣经提供了一个未来的盼望，那时雅伟将亲自擦去所有的眼泪，死亡、悲伤、哭泣和痛苦都将不复存在。这个应许在当前的悲痛中为我们的心提供了锚定。

title.en: Poland: Prime Minister Tusk defies anti-Ukrainian violence
title.zh: 波兰总理图斯克谴责反乌克兰暴力

summary.en: Anti-Ukrainian sentiment is increasing in Poland, leading to attacks against refugees from the war in Ukraine. Prime Minister Donald Tusk has publicly condemned this violence and issued a warning about the threat from Russia.
summary.zh: 波兰国内的反乌克兰情绪日益高涨，针对来自乌克兰战区的难民的袭击事件频发。总理唐纳德·图斯克公开谴责了这种暴力行为，并就俄罗斯的威胁发出了警告。

body.en:
Anti-Ukrainian sentiment in Poland is on the rise, with numerous attacks against refugees from the war in Ukraine. Prime Minister Donald Tusk has spoken out against the violence and warned of the danger from Russia.

The Polish leader didn't mince his words. "We must wage a resolute fight against this violence, because thugs, hooligans, and this culture of violence are becoming increasingly brazen and insolent — and also because they have received political support," Donald Tusk said on Tuesday, before a Polish cabinet meeting in Warsaw. The liberal-conservative prime minister said he deplored the fact that "more and more such incidents" are taking place all over Poland .

Tusk's comments came in response to an incident in Wroclaw two days earlier, in which three Polish men brutally beat up a young Ukrainian man and his girlfriend on the street. Cellphone videos show the attackers kicking the Ukrainian man as he lies on the ground. The woman was also hit, sustaining injuries to her neck and ear.

The attack came after an argument in a shop; the attackers took exception to the couple's Ukrainian accents. Polish police acted swiftly: Two of the attackers, both of whom have previous convictions, are already in custody, and a third is being sought.

Tusk warned that such incidents negatively impact Poland's image abroad. The country's reputation was greatly enhanced by its willingness to provide assistance after the start of Russia's full-scale war against Ukraine . This could be destroyed, said Tusk, "if we allow thugs, hooligans and common criminals to beat and humiliate people just because they have a slightly different accent."

Poland provided military and humanitarian assistance to its neighbor from the very beginning of Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022. It took in more than one million refugees from the war, and around 1.5 million Ukrainians are currently living in Poland. The majority of them work, pay taxes, and contribute to the Polish economy.

But four and a half years after the start of the war, the mood in Poland has changed. More and more often, Ukrainians are being verbally and physically attacked in public. Last Wednesday a Polish manager on a construction site in Skawina, near Krakow, was filmed aggressively insulting Ukrainian workers. In another incident on a local train near Warsaw, two drunken men shouted verbal abuse at a Ukrainian passenger. On July 11, a man on a bus in Bielsko-Biala insulted and threatened two Ukrainian girls who were trying to take a selfie. Even schoolchildren, including teenagers at a playground, have fallen victim to the new climate of hate.

body.en:

The flood has left 23 others injured, the ⁠official Xinhua news agency reported on Sunday.

The Shuangshimen Scenic Area, a popular tourist spot for camping, was hit by a flash flood on July 26, with state media initially reporting 10 deaths and 23 injuries.

The country's national commission for disaster prevention said it would oversee an investigation into the event.

Videos of the flood show a deluge ripping through a valley where several tents and cars were parked.

Authorities have warned of further landslides, including in ‌Dingxi, ​as heavy downpour continues in the annual flood season.

Beijing and Inner Mongolia also issued weather warnings on Sunday as China's ​weather observatory warned of heavy rain, high winds and thunderstorms across a large stretch of the country from ⁠the southwest ​to the northeast.

title.en: From petitions to memes: How students made dissent visible
title.zh: 从请愿到网络迷因：学生如何让异议显现

summary.en: Student movements throughout history, from imperial China to modern India, have consistently found new ways to express dissent and challenge established authority, adapting their methods to contemporary tools and symbols.
summary.zh: 从中国古代到当今印度，学生运动不断调整其工具和象征，以挑战权威，使异议得以显现。

body.en:
From imperial China to present-day India, student movements have repeatedly adapted the tools and symbols of their age to challenge authority.

On July 22, 2026, in rainy Mumbai, India , a casually dressed young woman stepped in front of a slow-moving police van carrying detained students. She placed her palm on the hood, forcing the vehicle to stop.

Mobile phones captured the moment from every angle. She too, raised her own phone and recorded the encounter. Within hours, the clip spread across India and beyond.

It became one of the defining visuals of the Cockroach Janta Party protests, a movement in which students demanded transparency and accountability, following leaks in India's medical entrance exams.

But the power of the moment lay not only in what she did, but in how quickly it was seen. A single gesture, a young woman confronting authority , became a symbol shared across millions of screens.

While the clip belongs to a generation raised on social media, the impulse behind it is much older.

From court petitions and revolutionary posters to photographs, umbrellas and memes, student movements have repeatedly adapted the tools and symbols available to them, turning them into vehicles for dissent.

Long before television or social media carried dissent across borders, students still found ways to make their grievances heard.

In Eastern Han China, for instance, scholars at the Imperial Academy (Taixue) aligned with reform-minded officials in opposing powerful eunuchs at court, whom many viewed as corrupt and politically overbearing.

They voiced their objections through public criticism, political networks and petitions.

In an era when political communication moved through official channels, petitions were among the established ways of bringing grievances before the throne. Written in formal language and delivered through the bureaucracy, they carried student concerns directly into the state's communication system.

In Paris in 1968, students challenged university authorities and a conservative postwar social order. As demonstrations spread across the French capital and drew in workers, one of the movement's most enduring contributions emerged from a basement workshop at the Ecole des Beaux-Arts.

The Atelier Populaire ("People's Workshop") printed thousands of posters during the protests, many of them overnight. Their bold graphics, silhouettes and slogans became the visual language of the movement. Produced collectively, many carried no individual author's name, helping transform protest into a shared public voice.

The posters and their messages could appear in dozens of places overnight, giving the protest a wide local visual presence.

Protests also became more impactful when images could be transmitted across borders.

title.en: US-China AI rivalry heats up as Chinese models gain ground
title.zh: 中美人工智能竞争加剧，中国模型迎头赶上

summary.en: China's AI platforms are rapidly advancing, narrowing the gap with US technology. This progress has led to renewed threats from the Trump administration, alongside accusations of intellectual property theft, raising concerns about escalating tensions between the two nations.

body.en:
China's AI platforms are rapidly closing the gap with their US counterparts, prompting fresh threats from the Trump administration. With accusations of intellectual property theft, could tensions boil over?

In what seems like the blink of an eye,  China has gone from being up to five years behind the United States in top-tier artificial intelligence (AI) to lagging by just a few months.

While US players, including Anthropic's Claude and OpenAI's ChatGPT , have spent hundreds of billions of dollars to push the frontier of AI, China has pursued a very different path .

Faced with US curbs on high-end chips that help AI to do its most advanced thinking, Chinese tech firms have prioritized dozens of open-source AI models built on "good enough"  technology .

These platforms, including DeepSeek, Alibaba's Qwen and Xiaomi's MiMo, are now widely deployed across Chinese businesses, government services and consumer devices.

In the latest sign of the gap closing, Chinese startup Moonshot AI last week unveiled Kimi K3, a model that rivals one of the most advanced AI models — Anthropic's Claude Fable 5 — on key benchmarks.

In some tests, Kimi K3 matches or even surpasses Claude with far less computing power and at a fraction of the cost. 

Global technology specialist Alvin W. Graylin thinks Kimi K3's arrival turns high-end AI from an expensive luxury into something practical and affordable.

"For 98% of customers, the 1 to 2% difference [in knowledge] isn't worth paying 10 to 20 times more."

China's latest advance has already drawn a strong reaction from Washington, with US President Donald Trump now threatening to block US access to Chinese AI models.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, meanwhile, warned earlier this week that the US could sanction Chinese models over alleged intellectual property (IP) theft.

Anthropic  and OpenAI have accused Chinese labs of using their models to train their own systems, a process known as distilling.

While distilling is a common practice by AI labs worldwide to a limited extent, the companies say their models have been bombarded with queries to harvest advanced reasoning. The White House warned in April that China was doing it on an "industrial scale."

Beijing has hit back, rejecting the accusations as baseless and calling US threats of sanctions and model bans "technological bullying" to contain China's rise.

Giulia Neaher, a research analyst at the Strategic Foresight Hub at the Washington-based Stimson Center think tank, downplayed the role of distilling in Kimi's progress.

Two people have been hospitalised after a building collapsed in central Sydney on Monday, emergency services said.

A spokesperson for New South Wales Ambulance said it was called to an address in Ultimo, a suburb around 2 km from the city's central business district, just before 11am.

Workers assessed seven patients at the scene. According to ABC News, one man in his 60s and another in his 30s were removed from the rubble and rushed to hospital in a serious condition.

One of the men was taken to St Vincent's Hospital Sydney. The other was taken to Royal Prince Alfred Hospital.

Fire and Rescue New South Wales (FRNSW) told ABC News that the building was a construction site. Nearby buildings, including an adjoining service station, have been evacuated.

summary.en: McDermott Aviation, an Australian helicopter provider, has expressed profound sadness following a firefighting tragedy in Greece, where helicopters leased by the company were involved as wildfires continue to spread across southern Europe.

body.en:
Two crew members have died after two helicopters — leased by Australian company McDermott Aviation — collided midair while battling wildfires in Greece on Sunday.

A Greek and a Danish national were killed in the crash over Psatha, an area west of Athens, according to Greece's fire service. Two crew members from Greece and Britain who were operating a separate helicopter were found alive.

Founder and president of McDermott Aviation, John McDermott said he was "deeply saddened" by news of the fatal collision.

"We are deeply saddened to confirm that the two crew members aboard one of the helicopters have lost their lives. The two crew members from the second helicopter are in the care of medical professionals.

"Our thoughts and deepest condolences are with the families, friends and colleagues of those affected by this tragic incident. Both crews were undertaking the critical work of supporting firefighting operations to help protect communities."

McDermott Aviation has reportedly operated in Greece for several years. The company said it is working closely with relevant authorities as they undertake an investigation into the cause of the incident.

Over the past decade, McDermott Aviation said it has engaged in around 10 to 12 international movements a year via sea and air freight. It also operates in New Caledonia, Papua New Guinea, Indonesia and the United States, which is currently experiencing wildfires in several western states.

Nikos Pagiotelis has been a volunteer firefighter in Greece for more than 20 years. He told SBS Greek about the moment he heard news of the crash over local radio.

"When you are inside the fire, and you are trying to help the people, you're trying to save the animals, save the forest. Then suddenly [you] hear that two helicopters have crashed a couple of miles near you — you can understand that something really hurts inside," Pagiotelis said.

"You can do nothing, you freeze for a little bit, and then you just continue your work. You continue to help people to honour the lives of the loss of two comrades."

In a statement on social media, Greek prime minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis also expressed his "sorrow for the tragic accident" and extended condolences to the families of the deceased firefighters.

"The loss of the Greek coordinator and the Danish pilot at the time they were attempting the major fire in Porto Gremeno fills us all with grief," Mitsotakis said.

Nearly 500 firefighters and 23 aircraft have been deployed to fight fires in Greece, which have been driven by high temperatures and gale-force winds.

title.en: Big tech companies could be hit with higher taxes if they don't strike deals with publishers
title.zh: 如果大型科技公司不与出版商达成协议，它们可能会面临更高的税收

summary.en: Tech giants criticised the previous draft laws released in April. What's changed?
summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及管家责任、供应与公共福祉。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Tech firms will pay a higher levy or strike more deals to avoid the charge under planned tweaks to an initiative to force them to hand over some of their revenue to media companies.

The proposed news bargaining incentive will push companies like Google, Meta and TikTok to strike commercial deals with news organisations to use the publishers' content on their platforms.

If deals are struck, the companies will pay a smaller share of their Australian advertising revenues to the government than if they refuse to reach agreements.

The levy will apply to tech giants with domestic revenues of $250 million or more, with any funds raised to be redistributed to the media sector.

But after a consultation period on the changes, which Labor hopes to legislate when parliament returns in Spring, elements of the incentive have been tipped further in favour of news publishers.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

The maximum levy that tech companies will pay on their revenue has been increased from 2.5 per cent from a previously proposed 2.25 per cent charge, the government revealed on Monday.

They will also have to strike at least six deals with publishers — rather than four — to fully discharge the liability.

But the revenue used to calculate the tech giants' payments will be limited to digital advertising income attributable to the Australian market.

Assistant Treasurer Daniel Mulino said the government had shown good faith in negotiating with both the platforms and media companies during the consultation process.

"Australian journalism is important to a well-functioning democracy and we want it to be sustainable now and into the future," he said.

"We want digital platforms to do deals with a diverse range of media organisations."

Approved agreements with large media companies would allow tech companies to offset 150 per cent of their liabilities, while deals with smaller firms attract a 200 per cent offset — up from 170 per cent under previous plans.

A professional networking platform carve-out that would have excluded LinkedIn has been scrapped.

The previous draft laws, released in April, were heavily criticised by the tech giants as "a government-mandated transfer of wealth from one industry to another".

title.en: Home prices fall across Australia as housing downturn takes hold
title.zh: 澳大利亚房价下跌，楼市低迷

summary.en: National home prices recorded their biggest monthly decline since 2022, with Sydney and Melbourne leading the falls.
summary.zh: 澳大利亚全国房价录得自2022年以来的最大月度跌幅，其中悉尼和墨尔本领跌。

body.en:
Australia's housing market downturn is spreading across the country as higher interest rates and changes to property taxes take hold.

Figures from property analytics company Cotality showed national home prices fell 0.7 per cent last month, the largest single-month decline since December 2022.

Annual growth has slowed to 5.3 per cent, well below the double-digit pace recorded earlier this year.

The country's largest property markets, Sydney and Melbourne, recorded declines of 1.4 per cent and 1.2 per cent respectively. Both cities are more than five per cent lower than recent peaks.

Brisbane and Adelaide, where prices have recently boomed, also recorded drops of 0.6 and 0.2 per cent respectively.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

In Perth, which has recorded the strongest year-on-year growth of any capital city at 21.8 per cent , prices were virtually flat, rising just 0.1 per cent.

"For buyers who remain in the market, lower competition and elevated stock levels (when compared with the start of the year) mean greater choice and more negotiating power," the property analytics firm said.

However, the fall in prices has been led by properties at the higher end of the market, providing little benefit to first home-buyers who are also grappling with lower borrowing capacity after three interest rate hikes this year.

Homes in the top quarter of the market lost 3.2 per cent of their value in the three months to July, compared to a 0.3 per cent gain in the lower-price tier.

Beyond the capital cities, the regional property market recorded a drop a 0.2 per cent — the first decline since January 2023.

"There remains a mismatch between the pricing expectations of buyers and sellers," Cotality head of research Gerard Burg said.

Consumer sentiment has also been soured by high living costs, uncertainty caused by the ongoing Middle East war and tax changes announced in the May budget.

"We have observed a deterioration in the flow of new listings across the country in recent weeks, led by Sydney, as potential vendors assess a weak market and choose to wait until conditions improve," Burg said.

Rental prices have continued to rise due to low vacancy rates. Burg said national median rents had risen by more than $200 a week in the last five years.

"Despite the tight market conditions, there are question marks about how much further rents can rise," he said.

body.en:
Strata and building managers are being contacted by the Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) ahead of the 2026 Census to help facilitate access to secure apartment buildings.

As president of the Strata Community Association of Australasia, Joshua Baldwin has been informing building managers about  the Census process .

He said while Census data collected by the ABS provides important insights into the nation's population and housing, coordinating access to secure-building apartments can become a "logistical nightmare".

Around 30,000 field staff have been hired by the ABS to ensure everyone in Australia is counted on 11 August. This involves delivering Census materials before Census night and following up with households that have not completed their Census after 11 August.

"We get a lot of questions as to why ... they need access onto our property and who is going to be [there]," Baldwin told SBS News.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

SBS News has seen correspondence between ABS staff and a Melbourne-based strata management firm.

The email outlines access arrangements for secure apartment buildings during Census activities, including requests for entry to prescribed premises between 8am and 8pm on weekdays and from 9am to 8pm on weekends. The ABS expects Census-related visits will conclude by the end of September.

In circumstances where Census staff cannot meet with onsite management to access buildings, the ABS may request temporary access arrangements, including apartment keys, fob cards or passcodes for secure areas.

Baldwin said he had heard of instances where "some Census officers have ... just straight up demanded access" to keys.

"Unfortunately, you know, we can't provide that access without the permission of the strata corporation," he said.

He acknowledged these interactions were rare and said, in most cases, facilitating building access was "quite fluid and quite easy".

To avoid handing over keys directly, Baldwin said some strata managers have established temporary box systems outside buildings, allowing authorised access while maintaining security arrangements.

For more than a century, the ABS has conducted the Census to provide a snapshot of Australia . The data collected helps inform understanding of the nation's population, housing and communities.

This includes information about Australian residents, international visitors and people on temporary visas.

summary.en: More Australians are delaying their retirement. For some, it's due to financial security. For others, it's more complicated.

body.en:

It was once a dream of many: work hard and retire in your 60s. Now, more Australians are employed into their 70s, 80s and even 90s. Insight meets those still working by choice, those who can't afford to stop, and asks what happens when you keep working later in life? Watch Insight episode Working Later in Life Tuesday 8.30pm on SBS or SBS On Demand.

Keiri Easdown retired as a professional dancer at the age of 45 when the work became too physically demanding. She never imagined that nearly three decades on, she would have tried four more careers and still be working.

"It was a rude shock really — having to do something like give up dancing," she tells Insight. "That was who I was; it was my life."

Leaving a physically demanding career — and one that also didn't allow her to save much money — the single mum had to retrain to earn a living and support her two children.

"Whatever I earned pretty much went out of the house; it paid the rent, it paid the bills for my children."

Since leaving behind her dance career, the 73-year-old has pivoted careers upwards of four times.

She's been an entertainment director at Gold Coast theme park Dreamworld, did some time in retail and corporate for a whitegoods company, and worked as a cleaner, before that became too physically taxing in her mid-60s.

On average, Australians plan to retire between their 65th and 66th birthdays, according to data released in 2024 by the Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS).

But Keiri, who has been working as a teacher aide at the school her daughter and son-in-law teach at since her late 60s, says she needs to keep working.

"I have very little in superannuation. As a dancer, we didn't earn much. We lived hand to mouth."

The average age of the 156,000 people who retired in the 2024-2025 financial year was 63.8, according to the ABS. Their exit from the workforce brought the nation's total number of retirees (aged 45 years and over) to 4.5 million.

The 2025 Household, Income and Labour Dynamics in Australia (HILDA) survey conducted by the University of Melbourne's Melbourne Institute found that, even though women are still retiring slightly earlier than men (a year on average), they are staying in the workforce longer than they once did.

In 2003, 69.5 per cent of women and 48.5 per cent of men in the 60-64 age group were retired. Twenty years later, these figures had dropped to 40.8 per cent and 27.4 per cent, respectively.

title.en: 'That was crazy': Australia's historic Commonwealth Games day ends with a bizarre twist
title.zh: “这太疯狂了”：澳大利亚历史性的英联邦运动会日以奇异的转折结束

summary.en: A midnight medal ceremony and a scaled-back format made for an unconventional Commonwealth Games in Glasgow.

body.en:
The Australian athletics team had its biggest one-day medal haul at the Commonwealth Games on Saturday, ending with a peculiar medal ceremony in a near-empty stadium.

Hours after the Games' athletics program ended, the Aussie men's sprinters were still waiting for their victory to be confirmed after protests over the other podium placings.

When the 4x100 relay team collected their medals in a makeshift ceremony along with the Canadian silver and Nigerian bronze medallists, the clock was ticking towards midnight.

The crowds at Glasgow's Scotstoun Stadium were long gone, with less than a hundred people remaining — mostly made up of Games officials, team staff, journalists and volunteers.

It was an odd ceremony for a major championship, with Australian winner Josh Azzopardi admitting with a smile: "That was crazy! We'd been waiting around not really knowing what was going to happen. It's definitely unique."

"We won gold, felt like it was ages ago now," said his teammate Lachlan Kennedy.

The holdup was the result of Canada's protests over their initial disqualification for a supposed illegal changeover, which was first upheld and then deliberated upon by the jury at great length until Canada was cleared for the silver.

It was an unusual conclusion to Australia's most successful athletics day ever at the Games, with a record haul of seven gold medals and 17 medals in total, including two events where the Aussies swept the podium.

Australia's previous record was set more than 70 years ago, with six gold medals and 11 medals in total in 1950.

It capped off the penultimate day of a stripped-back Games that had been quirky from the outset .

Victoria was originally supposed to host , but withdrew in 2023 due to rising costs. At the time, it prompted some to question the relevance of the Games and whether the event had a future at all.

The following year, organisers announced that Glasgow would step in as host city, with its Games to be supported in part by money from Victoria. The Victorian government had to pay a compensation of $589m including a $380 million settlement to cancel its hosting obligations.

While the Games has always had fewer sports and athletes than the Olympics, the 2026 event was even more pared back.

The 2022 Birmingham Games featured 20 sports and more than 5,000 athletes, while Glasgow hosted just 3,000 athletes competing in ten sports.

Some onlookers said the vibes in the city were vastly different to 2014, when it last hosted the Games.
